text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State-owned Air Zimbabwe this week flew two empty flights to and from Cyprus for President Robert Mugabe and his delegation's convenience, losing nearly Z$1 million in the process and leaving scores of passengers stranded.

- Officials from the International Monetary Fund, which withheld its support for Zimbabwe's economic reform programme after losing patience with persistent slippages in the southern African country's fiscal perfomance, will be in Zimbabwe early February for consultation on the long-stalled second phase of the programme.
- Zimbabwe has lost more than Z$1.08 billion in cross-border-transport revenue through unnecessary bureaucratic delays at the southern border post of Beitbridge.
- Zimbabwe will get over Z$600 million in grants and soft loans from the Italian government to finance various development projects, foreign affairs minister Stan Mudenge said in Rome on Thursday.

- The University of Zimbabwe has suspended three officials from the bursar's department, to pave the way for unfettered investigations into allegations that more than Z$8 million worth of payments were made to "ghost" students.
